segments.text: The source shows the same username query as before, but the page is now completely silent: it prints no message whether the user exists or not, so the only signal is timing.
I fetch the source and pull out the query.

I test the oracle: a true condition with a five second sleep takes about twenty seconds, because the query matches several rows and the sleep runs once per row, while a false condition returns in under half a second.
I test the length the same way: a password of thirty-two characters takes about twenty seconds, so the length is thirty-two.
I open vim and write the script:
The first chunk sets up the imports, the page URL, the credentials, and the start of timed, which measures how long a request takes.

The second chunk adds the condition test: it runs the request with curl and returns the elapsed time, then wraps the test in a scalar subquery, so a true answer costs one five second sleep instead of one per matched row, and treats anything over two and a half seconds as true.
The third chunk adds the loop: for each of the thirty-two positions, it binary searches the character code, asking whether the code is greater than or equal to a midpoint.
The last chunk prints each recovered character as it goes, and prints the final password at the end.
I run the script, and it prints the password one character at a time, finishing with all thirty-two characters.
